source.title: Demonstration of temperature-based quench detection on high-current insulated ReBCO coils made of LASSO cables

cases.source_conclusion: The study examines thermal coupling and electrical insulation of temperature-based detection methods on LASSO conductor samples of increasing size and stored energy.
blockers: Abstract/source metadata does not supply per-event latency distributions or false-positive/negative rates.
Extract raw time series, calibration, sensor placement, exact event definitions and uncertainty before quantitative detector ranking.
Do not infer high-energy coil or fusion magnet protection qualification from the demonstrated sample cases.

source.title: Microwave-based, sensor-free rapid quench detection for REBCO-based magnets and power transmission lines

blockers: The paper must be inspected for exact experimental versus simulated scope, operating conditions and measured observables.
No quantitative latency, false-alarm, missed-event, or detection-margin value is admitted from title/abstract alone.
Do not infer field-ready protection qualification.

source.title: Quench Protection in Insulated REBCO Conductors: Design Optimization and Fast Detection via REBCO SQD

compared_architectures: co-wound REBCO superconducting quench detector, electrically isolated and thermally coupled
cases.source_conclusion: The article reports a numerical proof of concept that stabilizer selection can keep hotspot temperature within a safe limit for its modelled events, and that an intentionally modified/deoxygenated REBCO SQD can transition at lower temperature for earlier detection.
blockers: Model assumptions, exact configurations, parameter values, uncertainty and source output traces must be extracted.
A modelled proof of concept is not a physical quench demonstration or magnet protection authorization.

source.title: Performance of the First 80 kA HTS CICC for High-Field Application in Future Fusion Reactors

blockers: 80 kA at 10.85 T and 4.5 K is the source-reported operating point; 46.5 kA at 20 T is a scaled/design projection, not the same measured test point.
Extract raw current/field/temperature and cyclic load curves, uncertainty, degradation and exact coil/test configuration before matched comparison.
This is a conductor prototype result, not a full magnet or fusion plant qualification.

source.title: Manufacturing and performance test of a 21.59 kA @77 K, self-field full-size REBCO-HFRC cable-in-conduit conductor

blockers: 77 K self-field performance is not directly comparable to 4.5 K high-field fusion operating points.
The source describes a design target for high-field operation; do not promote the self-field test to 20 T qualification.
Preserve conductor length, cable architecture, current definition and joint boundaries.

source.title: From critical temperature to engineering reality: A quantitative framework for assessing the translation gap in superconducting materials

source_synthesized_observations.qualifier: review's application/maturity framework, not independent certification
review-defined score, must reproduce scale and assumptions
review-defined score, not a universal materials ceiling

blockers: Manufacturing piece length and yield are review-synthesized estimates, not guaranteed values for every manufacturer or product generation.
Reproduce the score construction, application class and weighting before using the numeric score for design ranking.
Do not equate a review-assigned TRL with product certification or production capacity.

negative_controls.condition: Promote 77 K self-field 21.59 kA to a 20 T / 4.5 K rating.
Promote scaled 46.5 kA / 20 T design point to an 80 kA measured observation.
Compare critical current without tape count, cable architecture, temperature and field angle.
Rank materials by critical temperature alone.
Compare quench latency from non-identical event definitions or clocks.
Treat a simulated THEA hotspot as measured temperature.
Treat microwave sensor-free detection publication title as demonstrated low false-alarm protection.
Count a sensor failure as no quench or zero detection latency.
Omit AC losses, joint heating or refrigeration input from the system objective.
Use self-field Ic as high-field Ic or extrapolate outside field-angle envelope.
Treat a conductor prototype qualification as full magnet or fusion plant qualification.
Use review-synthesized TRL/yield/length as a vendor-guaranteed manufacturing specification.
